subject: securities-and-futures-act-2001
note: The open questions of row legalese-sonnet-5.5 (Cut A of the Securities and Futures Act 2001, Singapore), recorded on 2026-11-28 from the row's NOTES.md, the part notes under notes/ and the four reader triage files; it decides nothing new and none of its entries is a legal ruling. Entries are per open question, not per site: the sites are 266 tagged split sites and the rows of the readers' triage, and they stay in the tables of NOTES.md and notes/<part>-NOTES.md, which this register points at and does not reproduce. Each part keeps its own coverage table and fork lines in notes/<part>-NOTES.md. `taken` names what the encoding does where the parts split; a reading id that begins `perSite` is not a reading of the law but the encoding's behaviour while the question is open. Every entry has status `open`: it says the question is not settled, not that no answer was encoded. Where NOTES.md marks a decision as pending, the entry says who decided it and when, and that it awaits review. The text quoted is that of registers/source-bundle/SFA2001.txt, an informal consolidation that is not the official text.

readings.description: A failed gate answers `NOTHING`: a function named for a grant or a power that answers `JUST FALSE` when its gate fails reads as "may not". readings.description: For the pure gates only, the S1b ruling (2026S1bC; docs/ENCODING-GUIDE.md, section 5, 'Rulings on negatives and legal effects'), ruled 2026-11-21: a failed gate answers `JUST FALSE` where the function is a public body's power, a relief from an express bar or duty, or a gate the text closes, and `NOTHING` where it states a company's or person's liberty, standard or privilege with no bar to relieve. It turned four sites from `NOTHING` to `JUST FALSE`: s 139(6) and s 139(10) (sfaa), s 282AA(1) and s 281(1) (sfad). It governs only the functions that stay Boolean after the protocol split.

The Guide's grant ruling of 2026-11-12, limit 3, asks that a "may" function whose gate is "where", "when" or "upon" be listed in the row's fork register for the maintainer or a lawyer and not changed; for the pure gates of the two Singapore encodings the S1b ruling replaces that limit, and the protocol-shaped sites stay under it. This entry is that listing. notes/sfad-NOTES.md ('Marginal readings for a lawyer (sfad)', item 1) records that the Guide does not name "on application" and that it was read by analogy with "upon".

The grant ruling of 2026-11-12, on which readings `nothing` (limit 1) and the listing of the protocol-shaped sites (limit 3) rest, has not been confirmed by the maintainer: the Guide says of the grant ruling that it was "ruled by the coordinating session of the UK and Canada encodings on 2026-11-12; not confirmed by the maintainer" (docs/ENCODING-GUIDE.md, section 5, 'Rulings on negatives and legal effects'). The periods ruling of 2026-11-05, the delegated-definitions ruling of 2026-11-05 and the S1b ruling of 2026-11-21 are dated rulings recorded in the same section.

Thirteen of the 15 `ENCODER` lines of the readers' triage are placed with this question by NOTES.md ('The `ENCODER` lines (15)') and by the pull request body: a `where` or `if` gate read the other way from the part that wrote the function. None was applied. They are in two triage files only: group 3 has 12 (S31, S220, S523, S527, S561, S563, S564, S565, S566, S567, S568, S569; notes/reader-sfa-g3-triage.md) and group 1 has scenario 393 (s 276(7)(a); notes/reader-sfa-g1-triage.md); group 2 has no `ENCODER` line, and the one of group 4 is the naming defect recorded at F-sfa-239-3A.

Those 13 lines are not all "may" functions: s 197(3)(b) is a presumption stated with "if", s 218(4)(b) and s 218(4A) are conditions on what the prosecution or claimant proves, and the eight lines at s 234(1)(b)(ii), s 236D(1)(b)(ii), s 236G(1)(b)(ii) and s 236I(1)(b)(ii) are a "in the case where ... / in any other case" split of two comparison prices (notes/reader-sfa-g3-triage.md). Group 3 says that S220 and S527 have no fork line. This register does not count them among the 74 tagged sites, and NOTES.md does not say whether each is one.

Reader lines that the triage files label as a "may" gated by "where", "whenever", "with the consent of" or "after" are listed, by group, in F-sfa-reader-g1 to F-sfa-reader-g4. The line of group 2 at s 139(10) (#429) was recorded before the S1b ruling turned that function to JUST FALSE (sfaa-part8.l4:390, commit c0721dd59), so the triage line records NOTHING where the code now answers JUST FALSE.
The readers' triage verdicts, including that none of the 13 lines was applied, were decided by Claude 2026-11-19 (commit ea8692e7a), pending Meng's review.
See also F-sfa-offence-element (the type (i) sites).
